snip.t: Health promotion and education to improve knowledge, attitudes and behaviour of men and women about pregnancy.

What it achieves: through timely, evidence-based health promotion, disease prevention, screening and treatment, ANC reduces complications of pregnancy and childbirth, reduces stillbirths and perinatal deaths, and delivers integrated care throughout pregnancy.
Prevention and Health Promotion: Identifies risk factors, enabling targeted interventions (e.g., vaccination, lifestyle changes).
Health Promotion and Awareness: Screening programs raise awareness of preventable diseases, encouraging healthy behaviors and motivating individuals to seek preventive healthcare. *(5 marks)*

ai.subject: Public health
ai.summary: Health promotion is a proactive, community‑based approach that empowers individuals to adopt healthier behaviours and environments. It uses evidence‑based interventions to prevent disease, reduce risk factors, and improve overall well‑being.

sections.p: Health promotion is a set of planned, evidence‑based actions that enable people to increase control over health determinants and improve health outcomes.
b: Community engagement, education, policy change, environmental modification

sections.p: Unlike diseases, health promotion is not staged; its impact is measured by population health metrics such as reduced incidence, improved risk factor profiles, and increased health literacy.

Health‑related problems arise from modifiable risk factors—tobacco use, poor diet, physical inactivity, harmful alcohol use, unsafe sex, and environmental hazards. Socio‑economic and cultural contexts shape these behaviours.
b: Tobacco, alcohol, diet, inactivity, unsafe sex, pollution, poverty

sections.p: The ‘presentation’ is a population trend: rising rates of non‑communicable diseases, maternal mortality, or infectious disease outbreaks. Early signs include increased risk factor prevalence and low health literacy.
b: High smoking rates, low vaccination coverage, poor antenatal care attendance

sections.p: Health promotion relies on surveillance data, surveys, and screening tools to identify risk factors and target interventions.

t.b: High scores indicate need for targeted counseling

t.a: Screening programmes (e.g., blood pressure, HbA1c, cervical smear)

sections.p: When risk factors are unaddressed, complications include cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancers, maternal‑newborn morbidity, and infectious disease spread.
b: Hypertension, hyperglycaemia, anemia, unsafe sexual practices

sections.p: Management is a multi‑level strategy: individual counseling, community mobilization, policy advocacy, and environmental change. Interventions are chosen for effectiveness, feasibility, and cultural acceptability.
b: Individual education, group workshops, mass media campaigns, school curricula, workplace wellness, policy changes (taxes, smoke‑free laws), environmental modifications (clean water, safe roads)

t.b: Use counseling, nicotine replacement, or pharmacotherapy when available
Promote fruits, vegetables, whole grains, limit salt and sugar
Community exercise groups, safe walking paths

sections.p: Follow‑up involves monitoring population health indicators, evaluating intervention reach and effectiveness, and adjusting strategies. Prevention is ongoing, adapting to emerging risks.
b: Regular health surveys, program audits, policy reviews

sections.p: Health promotion is distinct from disease treatment or health education alone; it is a comprehensive, population‑based prevention strategy.
Surveillance data may under‑report risk behaviours due to stigma; screening tests may have false negatives in low‑resource settings.
Urgent care is needed for acute health crises, not for health promotion itself.

t.a: What is the main goal of health promotion?
t.b: To empower people to improve health and reduce disease risk through evidence‑based actions.

t.a: How does health promotion differ from health education?
t.b: Health education is a component; promotion includes policy, environment, and community change.
It ensures interventions are culturally appropriate, sustainable, and widely accepted.
